nodes.name: main.go
nodes.summary: Entrypoint for the factory command binary. It creates a background context, delegates command processing to the CLI package, and exits with the returned status.

nodes.name: cli.go
nodes.summary: Implements the factory command-line interface, including command dispatch, flag parsing, output formatting, and delegation to coordinator services.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Go's flag package with handler functions and explicit exit-status conventions.

nodes.name: config.go
nodes.summary: Defines host and repository YAML configuration models and provides loading, saving, path defaults, schema checks, and detailed validation for factory operation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses yaml.v3 decoding with explicit schema-version and policy validation.

nodes.name: Run
nodes.summary: Dispatches the requested CLI command, resolves the default host configuration path, and returns standardized exit statuses for usage and operational errors.

nodes.name: runBootstrapLabels
nodes.summary: Parses bootstrap-label flags and asks the factory service to create the repository's factory-owned labels, reporting the result to the user.

nodes.name: runIssue
nodes.summary: Parses an issue number and invokes the one-shot issue-claim workflow, returning usage or operational errors through the CLI output channels.

nodes.name: runAgent
nodes.summary: Parses agent-launch options, starts a factory agent invocation, and prints the resulting invocation packet and harness instructions.

nodes.name: runAgentReport
nodes.summary: Validates agent-report command arguments and submits the operator-provided report data to the factory service.

nodes.name: runDraftPullRequest
nodes.summary: Parses draft pull-request options and advances the selected run through checkpointing, gates, and draft pull-request creation.

nodes.name: runInit
nodes.summary: Parses initialization options, constructs a factory service, and initializes host or repository operational state.

nodes.name: runRegister
nodes.summary: Parses repository registration flags, builds the registration request, and invokes the factory registration workflow.

nodes.name: runStatus
nodes.summary: Loads factory status through the service layer and renders human-readable or JSON status output, including absent-run handling.

nodes.name: String
nodes.summary: Formats the custom string-list flag value as a comma-separated string for Go's flag.Value interface.

nodes.name: Set
nodes.summary: Appends a parsed command-line value to the custom string-list flag value.

nodes.name: HostConfig
nodes.summary: Represents the top-level host configuration, including its schema version and registered repositories.

nodes.name: RepositoryRegistration
nodes.summary: Stores host-level registration and runtime policy references for one managed repository.

nodes.name: GitHubConfig

nodes.name: PollingConfig
nodes.summary: Configures polling interval and backoff values for repository coordination.

nodes.name: CmuxConfig
nodes.summary: Configures the cmux control socket and workspace used by factory operations.

nodes.name: AuthenticationConfig

nodes.name: RepositoryConfig

nodes.name: GateConfig
nodes.summary: Describes one deterministic gate command, its timeout and blocking behavior, dependencies, and environment policy.

nodes.name: TimeoutConfig
nodes.summary: Groups configured time limits for setup, agent, gate, and review operations.

nodes.name: RetryLimits

nodes.name: TestPolicy
nodes.summary: Controls test enforcement mode and the permitted human or technical exemptions.

nodes.name: CacheConfig
nodes.summary: Describes a named worker cache path and whether the cache is read-only.

nodes.name: WorkerBuildConfig
nodes.summary: Specifies the worker image, digest, and build definition used for isolated work.

nodes.name: BaseSynchronization
nodes.summary: Selects whether and from which branch a worker synchronizes its base.

nodes.name: ValidationError

nodes.name: UnknownSchemaVersionError
nodes.summary: Reports a configuration schema version newer than the version supported by the binary.

nodes.name: ConfigFileError

nodes.name: NewHostConfig

nodes.name: LoadRepository

nodes.name: validateSchema

nodes.name: validateDuration

nodes.name: validateOptionalOverrides

nodes.name: TransitionRequest

nodes.name: BootstrapLabels

nodes.name: ClaimIssue

nodes.name: Invocation

tour.title: Factory Command Surface
tour.description: Start with the three command binaries to see how this project is entered: the main factory command delegates to the CLI, the report command serves worker-side reporting, and the attach command reconnects to a Docker worker. Together they reveal that the Software Factory is a supervised workflow with both coordinator-facing and worker-facing processes.
tour.languageLesson: Go command binaries commonly keep main.go thin: create process-level dependencies such as context, call a package-level service, and convert its returned error or status into the process exit result.

tour.title: CLI Dispatch Boundary
tour.description: The CLI translates arguments and flags into factory operations, including configuration, issue claiming, agent execution, gates, and draft pull requests. This is the first useful map of the orchestration layer because it connects the process entry point to the workflow capabilities without owning each capability’s implementation.

tour.title: Domain Model and Configuration
tour.description: Read the domain context alongside the checked-in repository configuration and configuration package to establish the vocabulary of runs, checkpoints, gates, workers, harnesses, reports, and credentials. The YAML file supplies the ordered gates, policies, timeouts, and worker image, while config.go turns those settings into validated host and repository models used by the rest of the system.
tour.languageLesson: Go configuration code often separates decoding from validation: unmarshalling creates a data shape, while explicit validation enforces cross-field and operational invariants before work begins.

tour.title: Factory Dependency Assembly
tour.description: The Factory service is the composition root for the workflow described in the earlier steps. It wires configuration, GitHub, SQLite storage, Git worktrees, Docker workers, terminal sessions, and the Codex harness behind injected adapters so higher-level orchestration can coordinate them without embedding infrastructure details.

tour.title: Claiming and Run State
tour.description: Issue claiming turns a repository issue into a durable supervised run: labels are bootstrapped, ownership is claimed, and stage and status transitions are persisted while GitHub statuses are synchronized. The store.go package is the recovery-oriented record of that lifecycle, providing SQLite migrations, validation, backups, duplicate reconciliation, and queries that let orchestration resume safely.

tour.title: Visible Agent Execution
tour.description: Building on the run state, agent.go coordinates a visible implementation-agent invocation: it resolves policy, prepares a worker and terminal surface, freezes invocation context, builds a prompt packet, and accepts the resulting structured report. prompt.go is the boundary that converts trusted context plus untrusted repository guidance into a versioned implementation-role prompt.
tour.languageLesson: Go interfaces make orchestration testable by allowing worker, terminal, and harness implementations to be replaced with fakes. The coordinator can then test policy and lifecycle decisions without starting Docker or a real terminal.

tour.title: Structured Report Protocol
tour.description: The worker-side report binary and report package close the agent loop opened in Step 6. reportcli.go translates flags and environment identity into one report, while report.go validates identity, outcome, paths, sizes, and worktree safety before the coordinator trusts the result or advances the run.
tour.languageLesson: A Go protocol package can make invalid states difficult to accept by centralizing parsing and validation at the boundary. Returning wrapped errors preserves the underlying cause while adding the operation that failed.

tour.title: Gates and Draft Pull Requests
tour.description: After an implementation report is accepted, gate.go and runner.go execute the configured setup and checkpoint commands inside an isolated worker and publish exact statuses. draft_pr.go then combines checkpointing, deterministic gates, worktree branch pushes, and idempotent pull-request creation or regeneration, turning a successful run into a reviewable artifact.

tour.title: Isolation and Git Adapters
tour.description: The workflow’s safety boundary is implemented by the worker and Git adapters: runtime.go controls hardened Docker lifecycle, mounts, commands, environments, and sessions, while worktree.go manages isolated branches, checkpoints, pushes, synchronization, inspection, and cleanup. These seams keep host-side coordination separate from the mutable workspace where agent and gate commands run.

tour.title: GitHub and Terminal Integration
tour.description: The external adapters complete the operational picture: github.go translates issue, pull-request, and exact commit-status operations through the host-side GitHub CLI, while terminal/runtime.go provides portable workspace and surface contracts over cmux. harness/codex.go composes those terminal and worker seams into a recoverable interactive Codex session, including constrained commands, prompts, notifications, and native session discovery.

tour.title: Architecture and Operating Rules
tour.description: Finish with the project’s written constraints: agent guidance defines repository conventions, the issue-tracker and triage documents explain how work is selected and labeled, and the ADR records the no-outbound-telemetry evaluation boundary. These documents turn the code tour into an operational understanding of how the factory should be used, changed, and audited.
